protocol.name: zelto_toplevel_capture_v1

description.summary: window snapshots for a task switcher

protocol.description:
An App Switcher shows a card per backgrounded window, and the card should show the WINDOW, not a generic app icon. No existing protocol can supply that. wlr-screencopy-v1 captures a wlr_output — but a backgrounded window is by definition not what is on the output, so capturing the output at the moment the switcher opens photographs the switcher itself.
This protocol inverts the timing. The compositor snapshots a window when the window LEAVES the foreground — the moment it still looks exactly as the user left it — keeps that image, and hands it to whoever asks later. The switcher therefore never captures anything; it only receives.
A capture object is keyed off the zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 the client already holds for the window, not off an app_id: app_id identifies an application, and one application may own several windows.
The image arrives as a sealed, read-only file descriptor the client maps directly. The compositor allocates a NEW fd for each snapshot rather than rewriting one buffer, so a client that is mid-animation over a mapped snapshot never has the pixels change underneath it.
A snapshot is a historical record, not a live view: it is by design STALE, showing the window as it was when it was last on screen. A client should show it anyway — a stale frame identifies a window far better than an icon — and expect no updates except a further `snapshot` event.

interface.name: zelto_toplevel_capture_manager_v1

description.summary: hand out capture objects for toplevels

interface.description: A global whose only job is to attach a capture object to a foreign toplevel handle.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroying the manager does not affect capture objects already created.

request.name: get_capture

description.summary: get the capture object for a toplevel

request.description:
Create a capture object for the window behind `toplevel`.
If the compositor already holds a snapshot of that window — the usual case, because the window was backgrounded before the switcher opened — it sends `snapshot` immediately. Otherwise the client hears nothing until the window is next backgrounded, and should show its fallback (the application's icon) in the meantime.

interface.name: zelto_toplevel_capture_v1
interface.description: Delivers snapshots of a single window as they are taken.

event.name: snapshot

description.summary: a snapshot of the window is available

event.description:
`fd` is a read-only, sealed file descriptor containing `height` rows of `stride` bytes. The client should mmap it PROT_READ / MAP_PRIVATE and must close it when done.
The fd is sealed against writing and shrinking, so the compositor cannot change or truncate it after the fact and the client can map it without risking a SIGBUS. Each event carries a fresh fd; a previously delivered one stays valid until the client closes it.
The image is usually a REDUCED-resolution copy of the window (a card in a switcher is far smaller than the window), so `width`/`height` describe the image and not the window. The aspect ratio is the window's, so a client should scale to fit rather than assume a size.

event.name: gone
event.description: The window this object captures has closed. No further snapshot events will arrive. Any snapshot already delivered remains valid and mapped — a switcher showing the card of an app that has just exited is exactly the case the snapshot exists for — but the client should expect nothing more and may destroy this object.
